role: AI-generated watercolor target, not native painter output
prompt:
Use case: style-transfer.
Asset type: AI-generated watercolor target for selection, one standalone artwork.
Input image: the source photograph is the composition and subject reference. Interpret it afresh as an ink-led field sketch. Medium detail comparable to the earlier h05-b study: identifiable silhouettes, main interior divisions and openings, only hints of ornament, grouped foliage, visible paper gaps. More ink work, without increasing decorative detail.
Primary request: Interpret the source as a real hand-made fast, loose observational ink-and-watercolor study, an unfinished sketch rather than a finished illustration. All variants begin with ink. The ink drawing must read clearly as a coherent drawing on its own, with hierarchy, structural junctions, selective interior divisions and shadow indications; retain substantial visible ink through the washes. Middle level of detail: neither a sparse silhouette sketch nor a dense rendering. Suggest rather than render ornament and texture.
Medium and surface: real neutral dark waterproof ink and transparent watercolor on white cold-press paper with visible natural paper tooth. Light comes from unpainted white paper; no white paint, gouache or opaque corrections.
Watercolor process: work light to dark: a loose first wash, then connected mid values, then a few decisive darks. Loaded round or mop for broad washes; let pigments mingle without repeated stirring. Wet-in-wet in visible sky, pale watery paint and irregular white cloud reserves; sky transitions should be fluid brush washes, never digital gradients. On dry paper use selective hard edges where light catches architecture and crisp recesses. Soften or lose other painted edges into adjacent washes. Natural localized blooms and granulation in pooled darks, transparent overlaps and occasional dry-brush skips; no uniform grain overlay. Group foliage into irregular masses with sky holes and a few branch lines; no individual leaf inventory.
Composition: keep the photo's composition, viewpoint, relative scale and principal silhouettes; simplify within a landscape 3:2 frame. Slight irregular vignetting into unpainted paper around the edges, no decorative border. Artwork alone, straight on; no desk, frame, hands, tools, labels, captions or signature.
Avoid: photographic detail, a watercolor filter applied to a photo, digital gradients, airbrush shading, vector-perfect outlines, outlines on every painted boundary, oversaturation, exhaustive bricks/windows/leaves, uniform stippling, polished illustration. The drawing should be confident, slightly irregular and incomplete at peripheral edges.
Scene and structural invariants: A close frontal Gothic stone facade with a central pointed arched gateway, partly open patterned iron gate on the left side of the opening, and a view into a bright courtyard through the right side. Keep upper window groups, left paired windows, right projecting window bay, diagonal tree shadows, and the converging paved path between low green planting beds. Main ink work describes arch moulding, gate framework with only a few pattern hints, window groups, facade junctions and path perspective. Suggest selected masonry fragments rather than a wall-wide grid. Preserve the bright slit through the gate.
Region techniques: There is no broad sky in this source; do not invent one. Lay one loose pale warm stone wash around paper lights, then connected cool-gray diagonal tree-shadow shapes with both soft and hard sections. Dry-paper arch recess darks and muted green planting washes. Preserve sunlit arch edges and inner courtyard light as paper.
Ink and wash sequence: Variant a — PEN-AND-INK DRAWING FIRST, THEN QUICK WASHES. Start on dry paper with a coherent waterproof dip-pen or nib-pen drawing, varied thin and heavier line weights, interrupted contour strokes, a little purposeful hatching in key shadow planes and structural recesses. The drawing has enough interior structure to stand on its own. After ink sets, lay quick transparent washes over and beyond some lines, then mid values and a few darks. Keep the ink plainly visible. Hatching is local and light, not a blanket texture. This is a lively sketchbook study.
Critical detail ceiling: Match a medium-detail field sketch's number and scale of descriptive marks. Stronger ink means darker and more varied existing structural strokes, not extra ornament. Reduce small tracery, moulding subdivisions and canopy marks; omit most carvings and all systematic masonry grids. Keep open spaces between pen marks. Retain only a handful of suggested tracery lines at the focus. The dominant impression is a brisk field study, with broad washes and visibly unfinished peripheral drawing.
HIGHEST PRIORITY FOR THIS CLOSE-UP: leave MOST wall areas free of masonry lines and separate stone dabs. Represent the wall with broad connected warm-gray washes and broad diagonal shadow gestures; just 8–12 scattered broken stone-joint hints across the entire facade, no brick or stone grid. Upper windows use a few main mullions, no little pane lattice. The gate is one dark transparent shape, ink main frame, only 3–5 abstract curls to suggest its pattern; leave the rest unrendered. Ornament under the upper windows is omitted. No repetitive little motifs. Keep a medium amount of structural linework concentrated at the arch and major window/plane junctions. Wash gestures must be larger than individual stones. The result is a quick ink field study with half-described surroundings, at a middle level of detail.
